title: Can You Eat Your Favorite Candy on Your Favorite Day?
summary: Given an array candiesCount indicating the number of each type of candy, and an array of queries specifying a favorite candy type, a favorite day, and a daily cap, determine whether it is possible to eat a candy of the specified type on the given day without exceeding the daily cap on any day.
statement: Given an array candiesCount indicating the number of each type of candy, and an array of queries specifying a favorite candy type, a favorite day, and a daily cap, determine whether it is possible to eat a candy of the specified type on the given day without exceeding the daily cap on any day. Return a boolean array where each element indicates whether the condition is met for the corresponding query.
constraints: Eat at least one candy daily, never exceed the query cap, and finish each candy type before starting the next.
For [type,day,cap], report whether a candy of that type can be eaten on that zero-based day.
hints: By a given day, total candies eaten can be any integer from day+1 through (day+1)*cap.
Compare that attainable interval with the one-based index interval occupied by the requested type.
Let before be prior-type count and through include this type; require day+1<=through and (day+1)*cap>before.
Two integer intervals overlap exactly under those inequalities, which is equivalent to eating the requested type that day.
editorial: Two integer intervals overlap exactly under those inequalities, which is equivalent to eating the requested type that day.

tests.explanation: The possible-consumption interval overlaps type zero and type two for the first and third queries, but cannot reach type four by day two.
The only type can be eaten on days zero through four, but is exhausted before day five.
